title: Stone Game V
summary: Alice arranges stones in a row with values in stoneValue.
statement: Alice arranges stones in a row with values in stoneValue. In each round, she splits the row into two non-empty parts. Bob sums the values of each part and discards the higher sum, adding the lower sum to Alice's score. If the sums are equal, Alice chooses which part to discard. The game concludes when only one stone remains. Alice starts with a score of zero and aims to maximize her score.
constraints: Split the current row into two non-empty parts; the higher-sum part is discarded and the lower sum is scored.
On equal sums, choose which part remains; maximize the final accumulated score.
hints: Use prefix sums for interval totals and memoize the best score for each interval.
Try every split and add the smaller side’s sum to the optimal continuation on that side.
When sums tie, consider continuing on either side.
Every play sequence begins with exactly one split, so maximizing these complete continuations yields optimal play.
